source.author: verg
source.text: Pandite nunc Helicona, deae, cantusque movete, qui bello exciti reges, quae quemque secutae complerint campos acies, quibus Itala iam tum floruerit terra alma viris, quibus arserit armis.
source.text_original: Pandite nunc Helicona, deae, cantusque movete, / qui bello exciti reges, quae quemque secutae / complerint campos acies, quibus Itala iam tum / floruerit terra alma viris, quibus arserit armis.
source.text_english: Now, goddesses, open Helicon and move the song: what kings, roused to war, what armies each followed filled the plains, with what men the nourishing land of Italy already then flourished, with what arms it burned.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: iam pridem regio, quae virginis aequor ad Helles et Tanain tenus immenso descendit ab Euro, undat equis floretque viris, nec tollere contra ulla pares animos nomenque capessere bellis ausa manus; sic fata, locos sic ipse fovebam.
reuse.text_original: iam pridem regio, quae virginis aequor ad Helles / et Tanain tenus immenso descendit ab Euro, / undat equis floretque viris, nec tollere contra / ulla pares animos nomenque capessere bellis / ausa manus; sic fata, locos sic ipse fovebam.
reuse.text_english: Long since the realm which from the great east wind slopes down to the seas of Helles and Tanais, where it is full of horses and flourishes with men, had no band that dared to lift up against it equal spirits or to take up arms in war; so had the fates decreed, and so I myself cherished those regions.
